subject.title: [Bug]: Trajectory files fed back as context cause unbounded token consumption and unexpected API billing

question: Is the current source and release guardrail evidence enough to close this high-billing trajectory-context report, or should OpenClaw require a fresh Windows/provider proof first?
rationale: This is a real billing/session-state report, but the remaining gap is proof sufficiency rather than a narrow source defect the review can safely patch from inspection alone.

options.title: Require live proof first
options.body: Keep this open until a current-main Windows or equivalent provider run proves whether large trajectory sidecars enter fresh-session context.

options.title: Close as source-fixed
options.body: Close based on the current trajectory filters and reseed/session guardrails, accepting that the exact reported billing path was not reproven.

options.title: Add stricter guardrails
options.body: Keep open for a maintainer-sponsored hardening change that makes trajectory sidecar exclusion explicit at every context ingestion boundary.

recommendation.title: Require live proof first
recommendation.body: Keep this open until a current-main Windows or equivalent provider run proves whether large trajectory sidecars enter fresh-session context.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is on the trajectory artifact classifier and cleanup code that would anchor the proof or hardening decision.
